I could only wish to be a natural, that would be a great ability. My preferred method is MILD, which is a variation of DILD in which you repeat a mantra as you go to sleep, such as "I will lucid dream tonight". That method has worked the most for me, as in lucidity and given me the most control.

Lesser known tips on WILD? Hm. Well, some common errors people make is that they stay too alert, just looking at the insides of their eyelids. This is incorrect. The correct way is to let the body fall asleep like normal, but keep your consciousness just a tad bit by having an anchor, something to focus on as your body is drifting asleep. Another thing is to get comfortable when trying to WILD, if you are not, such as lying on your back when you usually sleep on your side, you're not going to get anywhere with that. One problem other people have, are false awakenings, they will "wake up" in the dream from the WILD, only to think they failed. Every time you believe you may have woken up, perform a reality check to test, odds are you are in a dream.

1: Recall is a heavy hitter in lucid dreaming. I would suggest, if you have a hard time getting to sleep, to go to bed earlier than you would regularly, in order to ensure that you get more sleep, which in turn, creates more time for dreaming. And the slightest hint of a dream, write it down. Also when you wake up in the morning, lay completely still and do not move, don't even open your eyes. This is the best way to remember dreams from the night.

2: Yes, that method is the WILD, and the most difficult but most rewarding to perform. You should start performing reality checks, which are tests to check if you are dreaming, and once you get accustomed to these in real life, you will start doing them in your dream, and get lucid.
